gold_with_text_not_included.reason: I1-I5 met: task fMRI in 14 healthy girls using instructed distancing to reduce sadness elicited by film excerpts, with within-group emotion/regulation main effects and their interaction. I6 not met because qualifying whole-brain peak evidence was not demonstrated. The stated corrected inference uses a priori ROI small-volume correction; reported main-effect coordinates and Table 1 do not identify peaks from a whole-brain-thresholded analysis. Although the text says a whole-brain search was carried out, no corresponding threshold or clearly attributable whole-brain peak results are reported. E2 remains unclear given that statement. The childhood sample and visual films qualify; the within-subject interaction is not a between-group-only analysis.

Incomplete source: only the abstract and publisher landing-page material are present; Methods, Results and coordinate tables are missing. The abstract supports task fMRI with instructed regulation of responses to pictures (I1-I3) and within-task regulation effects (I5), but sample eligibility (I4) and whole-brain peak reporting (I6) remain unassessable. Return for full-text retrieval rather than exclude.

I6 not met: the whole-brain random-effects analyses report Talairach centers of mass (Table 2), with maximum t statistics given separately; peak coordinates are not demonstrated. I1-I5 met: healthy adults performed instructed reality checking during anticipation of IAPS images, with within-group negative/unknown-versus-neutral contrasts. E1-E5 do not apply. The basic-group sample was reported previously, but sample overlap is not an exclusion criterion.

I6 is not demonstrated: original Tables 1 and 2 label their Talairach coordinates as cluster centers, not activation peaks. Descriptions of supplementary task maps also do not establish peak coordinates. I1-I5 are met: task fMRI used instructed reappraisal of IAPS pictures, control-group task responses are plotted separately, and a whole-sample Reduce-Maintain effect is reported. Whole-brain task analyses are present, so E2-E4 do not apply.

I3 not met: participants regulated responses to verbal ANET scripts consisting of three to four sentences. These word/sentence stimuli are expressly excluded. I1, I2, I4 and I5 are met by task fMRI with instructed up- and down-regulation and separately reported healthy-control task effects. Whole-brain within-group analyses are described, with results assigned to supplementary Table S3 and MNI normalization (I6).

Excluded because all fMRI analyses use anatomically defined ROIs in the amygdala and specified regulation-network regions (E2 met); no accompanying whole-brain task activation map is demonstrated (I6 not_met). Task fMRI, instructed reappraisal/distraction of emotional IAPS images, separately reported healthy-control results, and within-group emotion/regulation contrasts meet I1-I5. Separate one-sample analyses and their results mean E4 does not apply.

I6 not met: standard-space peak-coordinate reporting was not demonstrated in the supplied full text and tables. Whole-brain task effects are explicitly referenced in supplementary Table S3 and Figures S5–S6, but their coordinates and anatomical space are not provided or described in the available inputs. I1–I5 are met: community adults performed instructed reappraisal of negative images, with regulation and viewing contrasts reported. E2 does not apply because accompanying whole-brain analyses are explicitly reported.

I6 not demonstrated: group-level whole-brain task effects and peak xyz coordinates are reported in Tables 1–2, but the supplied text and tables do not identify a standard anatomical coordinate space. Acquisition and processing details are deferred to supplementary material absent from the supplied inputs. I1–I5 are met: 19 healthy children performed instructed positive reappraisal of sad photographs during fMRI, with reappraise sad versus view sad and sad versus neutral effects. E1–E5 do not apply.

All contrasts used an explicit PFC/anterior cingulate/amygdala mask (E2 met; I6 not met). Tables 2-3 report Talairach coordinates from these restricted analyses; no whole-brain map is reported. Task fMRI, instructed reappraisal/selective attention, visual film clips, and nonclinical younger/older participants satisfy I1-I4. Within-group regulation versus passive-viewing effects satisfy I5, so E4 does not apply.

Healthy participants performed instructed cognitive reappraisal of aversive IAPS images during fMRI (I1-I4). The localizer group analysis reports reappraisal-versus-viewing and reverse contrasts with Talairach foci in Table 2 (I5). However, acquisition explicitly provided only limited coverage of high parietal cortices and the cerebellum. Although the authors call the voxelwise GLM whole-brain, no accompanying analysis with full brain coverage is demonstrated (I6 not met; E2 met). The localizer task effects mean this is neither connectivity-only nor between-group-only research (E3-E4).

Task fMRI uses instructed acceptance and reappraisal of sad pictures, with separately reported healthy-control and remitted-depression task contrasts (I1-I5 met). However, reported inference uses an a priori frontal-lobe/bilateral-amygdala mask for small-volume correction. Tables 3-5 contain MNI peaks for these restricted analyses, with no separately reported unrestricted whole-brain result. Whole-brain image acquisition and model fitting do not establish whole-brain statistical inference: I6 is not demonstrated and E2 applies. The paper notes that reappraise-versus-view results from these data were reported previously; overlap is not itself an exclusion criterion.

I1–I5 met: original task fMRI of 15 meditation practitioners instructed to use positive reappraisal or compassion to regulate responses to distressing films, with within-sample regulation and viewing contrasts. E5 does not apply because emotional modulation is explicitly instructed. Whole-brain group maps are described in Figures 2–3, and analysis uses an MNI-projected template. However, peak coordinates in standard space are not demonstrated in the supplied text or tables: activation tables are referenced but their contents are absent and the tables directory is empty. I6 is therefore not_met under the strict full-text rule; this is not an ROI-only exclusion.

I1-I5 met: original task fMRI in 20 healthy women instructs self-distancing from aversive IAPS pictures and reports within-sample Distance/Attend activation contrasts. I6 is not demonstrated: group-level whole-brain activation and MNI normalization are described, but no peak coordinates for those activation maps are supplied or explicitly identified as reported. The cited supplementary Table S2 is unavailable in the assigned tables directory, and the figure placeholders have no coordinate-bearing captions. The explicit MNI triplet belongs to a small-volume-corrected PPI result, which cannot establish I6. E2 and E3 do not apply because whole-brain task activation analyses accompany the connectivity analysis.
